newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN UIC unit posts H1 loss.
newsitem.headline: GAN UIC unit posts H1 loss.

text.p: (All figures in millions of French francs)

NOTE - Union Industrielle de Credit (UIC), the property financing unit of insurer GAN, noted in a statement its 1995 net consolidated loss was 1.58 billion francs. It said as a result of "a property situation that remains depressed, half year results were marked by the weight of provisions totalling 621 million francs". UIC added details of a planned recapitalisation announced in April would be finalised in the next few weeks.
UIC, whose parent GAN is hoping to be privatised in 1997, said the recapitalisation would total 800 million francs.

A spokeswoman for UIC said UIC does not give half year comparisons but rather divides the year in half to arrive at a comparative figure. The 1995 net attributable profit totalled 1.68 billion francs, she said. Full-year provisions for 1995 totalled 1.07 billion francs, she said.
It said that UIC had a gross operating loss of 70 million francs. The net banking income was 175 million francs.

As of June 30, net loans totalled 14 billion francs, down 1.3 billion francs. This fall included a one billion franc reduction in loans to real estate developers. Total loans to developers fell to 3.3 billion francs from 4.3 billion francs and were provisioned at a rate of 64.5 percent.

The property financing company, originally part of GAN's CIC banking arm, has been at the centre of GAN's financial woes during the last three years after falling victim to a slump in the French property market.
The spokeswoman said worst hit was the commercial property market. "The prices continue to fall regularly," she said.
